metadata.title: Understand Context
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Fully understand the context, sources, and requirements for a task or process. Use at the beginning of any process to gather parameters, identify sources, understand requirements, and document constraints.

output.description: Context documentation in step{N}-context.md file and memory.json reference

specificActions: Follow the substeps below in sequence

Workflow: gather parameters → identify sources → clarify requirements → understand success criteria → document constraints → verify completeness → request missing info (if needed) → create context file → update memory reference
MANDATORY: Always create step{N}-context.md file with full context documentation - do NOT present context inline in conversation
Memory should only contain a reference: '**Detailed Context**: See [`step{N}-context.md`](./step{N}-context.md)'
Context file provides better readability for approval checkpoints

create: step{N}-context.md (MANDATORY - full context documentation for approval)

tools: read_file - read process.json parameters and understand process description
codebase_search - find relevant files or areas when scope is mentioned
grep - search for specific patterns or references
list_dir - explore directory structures if needed
bestPractices: Never assume context - always verify parameters and requirements
Ask clarifying questions if anything is ambiguous
Organize context information clearly in memory.json
Use specific, actionable questions when requesting missing information
Wait for user answers before proceeding if context is incomplete
Verify context completeness before moving to next step
VERIFY FILE EXISTENCE: Before claiming files exist or are missing, use Glob or list_dir to verify. Never make claims about codebase state without tool-based verification.

CHECK SOURCE REPOS: When investigating framework internals (templates, steps, configuration), check BOTH the locally synced copy (~/.claude/agentic-processes/) AND the source git repositories (listed in additional working directories or template-sources config). The synced copy may be stale or incomplete — the source repo is the ground truth.
DOCUMENTATION FIRST: Read existing project documentation (README.md, docs/, etc.) before creating context analysis. Existing docs may already answer questions or provide critical context.

REWRITE ON SCOPE CHANGE: When the user expands or significantly modifies the scope during review (e.g., adds new research areas, changes boundaries), rewrite the context document from scratch with a unified voice. Do NOT patch new content into the existing document — this creates visible seams and forces the user to request a rewrite.

AVOID REDUNDANT INFRASTRUCTURE FILES: When designing multi-file architectures, check whether proposed infrastructure/metadata files duplicate data already available in existing files (e.g., process.json already contains process metadata). Only introduce new files when they serve a purpose not already covered.

substeps.name: Gather Process Parameters
substeps.description: Read process.json parameters to extract all parameters from the process context
actions: Read process.json parameters to extract all parameters from the process context
Identify required vs optional parameters
Note any parameter placeholders (e.g., {{parameterName}}) that need substitution
Document parameter values and their meanings
Check if parameters are clear or need clarification

substeps.name: Identify Information Sources
substeps.description: Determine what files, directories, or documentation need to be reviewed
actions: FIRST: Read existing project documentation (README.md, docs/ directory) - these often contain critical context that should inform analysis
Determine what files, directories, or documentation need to be reviewed
Use Glob or list_dir to VERIFY which files/directories actually exist before claiming their presence or absence
Use codebase_search to find relevant codebase areas if scope is mentioned
Use read_file to examine process description and context
List external resources if applicable (documentation, APIs, etc.)
When investigating framework files (templates, steps, config), also check source git repositories — not just the locally synced copy
Note any missing sources that cannot be located (only after verification with Glob/list_dir and source repo check)

CONSUMER LAYER IDENTIFICATION: When the concept involves data structures, APIs, or shared types, proactively identify all consumer layers (UI apps, downstream services, CLI tools, scripts) that read or display the data. Check additional working directories and project paths for consumer codebases. Do NOT wait for the user to expand scope — include consumers in the initial analysis.

substeps.name: Clarify Requirements
substeps.description: Extract and document requirements from process description
actions: Extract explicit requirements from process description in process.json parameters
Identify implicit requirements from context parameters
Document what needs to be accomplished
Note any ambiguous requirements that need clarification
Understand the scope and boundaries of the work

substeps.name: Surface and verify assumptions
substeps.description: Present key assumptions to user for early validation before deep analysis
actions: Based on parameters, sources, and requirements gathered so far, list the top 3-5 assumptions the agent has formed about scope (what is included/excluded), architecture (technical approach, patterns, structure), and boundaries (constraints, limitations, interfaces)
Present these assumptions to the user clearly, numbered and categorized, requesting confirmation or correction for each
If the user corrects any assumptions, log each correction as a user interaction with forImprovementStep: true so the continuous-improvement step can identify systemic assumption patterns

After any user correction, immediately rewrite ALL affected sections of existing artifacts (context files, tables, classification labels). Do NOT patch individual lines — rewrite the affected sections from scratch to ensure full consistency. Verify no stale values remain.
Adjust the analysis direction based on any corrections before proceeding to deeper analysis (success criteria, constraints)

MIGRATION STRATEGY: When the concept involves restructuring existing patterns, replacing fields, or moving responsibilities, explicitly ask the user about migration strategy as one of the assumptions: (a) Clean migration — replace existing patterns entirely, no backward compatibility, (b) Gradual migration — maintain backward compatibility during transition. Do NOT default to either option — present both and ask.
Output: '✓ Assumptions validated with user - [N] confirmed, [M] corrected'

substeps.name: Understand Success Criteria
substeps.description: Identify how success will be measured
actions: Identify how success will be measured
Document expected outcomes
Note any acceptance criteria from process parameters
Understand verification methods
Clarify what 'done' means for this task

substeps.name: Document Constraints
substeps.description: Identify and document all constraints and limitations
actions: Identify technical constraints (libraries, frameworks, patterns to use)
Note time or resource constraints if mentioned
Document any limitations or restrictions
Record any dependencies that must be satisfied
Note any assumptions being made

substeps.name: Verify Context Completeness
substeps.description: Check if all necessary information is available
actions: Check if all necessary information is available
Identify any gaps in understanding
Verify that success criteria are clear
Ensure requirements are unambiguous
Confirm that information sources are identified

substeps.name: Request Missing Information
substeps.description: If context is incomplete, formulate specific questions for missing information
actions: If context is incomplete, identify what's missing
Formulate specific questions with format: Q1: [question], Context: [why needed], Category: [Parameters/Sources/Requirements/Success Criteria/Constraints]
Question categories: Parameters (missing values), Sources (unidentified files), Requirements (ambiguous), Success Criteria (undefined), Constraints (unknown limitations)
Present questions to user clearly
Wait for responses before proceeding
Update context documentation with answers once provided
Re-verify context completeness after receiving answers

substeps.name: Create Context File and Update Memory
substeps.description: Create step{N}-context.md with full documentation, update memory.json with reference
actions: MANDATORY: Create step{N}-context.md file in process directory with full context documentation
File structure: Concept Overview, Current State, Target State, Target Files, Requirements, Success Criteria, Constraints, Questions/Gaps
Organize clearly with headers and tables for readability
Record: reference only: '**Detailed Context**: See [`step{N}-context.md`](./step{N}-context.md)'
Do NOT put detailed context inline in conversation - the file IS the deliverable for approval

VERIFY BEFORE APPROVAL: Before proceeding to the approval checkpoint, re-read the context file and confirm it incorporates ALL user answers, corrections, and scope changes from substep 4 and substep 8. Do NOT present a stale context file for approval.
Output: '✓ Created step{N}-context.md' - DO NOT proceed to approval checkpoint without this verification

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
substeps.description: Verify principles were followed in this step
actions: Verify: Was log.json updated for any user interactions?
Verify: Were mandatory actions confirmed with output?

Log problems: If any problems, errors, workarounds, or unexpected situations were encountered during this step, log them via add-log-entry --problems '["description of problem 1", ...]'. This feeds the continuous-improvement step's analysis.
Output: '✓ Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Linear flow through substeps 1-4 (including assumption validation), then substeps 5-7, conditional substep 8 if gaps found, then substep 9. If substep 8 executed, return to substep 3 after receiving answers.

fields: Information Produced: Process parameters, Information sources, Requirements, Success criteria, Constraints
Decisions Made: Clarifications, Assumptions, Information source selections
Notes: Q&A questions and answers, References to process parameters, Gaps needing clarification
